pages.heading: Month by month
pages.body: One good moment for every month, from January to November. Some made the news. Some made us smile. All of them are ours.

pages.heading: A 15 year old from Tralee wins the Young Scientist
pages.body: The year opened with a teenager from Tralee taking the Stripe Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition. Her project, GlioScope, uses AI to spot brain tumour mutations from MRI scans, so doctors can avoid invasive sampling. Almost 2,000 entries came in and 550 reached final judging. She wins 7,500 euro and a trip to Kiel for the EU contest. Fourth year, and already ahead of us.

pages.heading: Ben Lynch skis into an Olympic final
pages.body: Ireland is not famous for ski slopes, so this one felt special. On 20 February, Ben Lynch, 23, finished eighth in the halfpipe final at the Winter Olympics in Livigno, with a score of 75.00. He was the first Irish skier to qualify for an Olympic final, and it was his Olympic debut. Jessie Buckley also won a BAFTA that month, but more on her next.

pages.heading: Jessie Buckley wins Best Actress at the Oscars
pages.body: On 15 March Jessie Buckley won the Oscar for Best Actress for Hamnet. The Irish Times called her Ireland's first ever best actress winner. Brenda Fricker won in 1990, but that was the supporting category, so this is a fresh first. Richard Baneham also collected a third Oscar that night, for visual effects. Not a bad evening for the home team.

pages.heading: Rory McIlroy wins the Masters again
pages.body: Rory McIlroy kept the Green Jacket. On Sunday 12 April he won the Masters for the second year in a row, finishing twelve under par after a closing round of 71 and beating Scottie Scheffler by one shot. It is his sixth major. The same month, Dermot Kennedy's album The Weight of the Woods landed at number one in Ireland, his third in a row.

pages.heading: Irish students win on the world stage
pages.body: Two prizes in one week. On 13 May, TU Dublin's SolHex, four third year Product Design students, won the NIBS Worldwide Business Plan Competition online finals with a habit support system called Daylight. Two days before, a Letterkenny Leaving Cert student was named European winner of the Earth Prize for Eco Purge, a plastic that helps break down microplastics.

pages.heading: Irish creatives take a top prize at Cannes Lions
pages.body: Ireland's ad people went to Cannes and came home with gold. Publicis Dublin won a Grand Prix for the strategy behind Heineken Ireland's The Pub That Refused To Die, Ireland's third ever. Better still for young talent, two junior creatives at TBWA Ireland won gold in Young Lions Print, with just 24 hours to make a water safety ad.

pages.heading: Mayo end a 75 year wait
pages.body: Seventy five years of waiting ended on 26 July. Mayo beat Kerry by one goal and twenty points to one goal and seventeen in the All-Ireland football final at Croke Park. They trailed by six in the 21st minute and led from the 37th. It is their fourth title and their first since 1951. Limerick won the hurling title a week earlier, on 19 July.

pages.heading: Mark English wins European gold in Birmingham
pages.body: On 13 August at the European Championships in Birmingham, Mark English won the 800m in 1:45.26, the first Irish man to win an individual European outdoor gold. Rhasidat Adeleke then took 200m silver in an Irish record of 22.28. Two days later Kate O'Connor won heptathlon gold with 6,751 points, another Irish record.

pages.heading: Katie Taylor says goodbye at Croke Park
pages.body: On 5 September, more than 80,000 people filled Croke Park to watch Katie Taylor beat France's Flora Pili on a unanimous decision. She retired as a three times undisputed world champion. Earlier that week, Met Éireann said the summer had provisionally been the warmest on record, at 16.28 degrees. A warm summer and a warm send off.

pages.heading: Fontaines D.C. go to number one
pages.body: Dublin band Fontaines D.C. reached number one with their fifth album, Dopamine Chamber, their second chart topper after Skinty Fia. It sold over 70,000 chart units in its first week, the third biggest opening week for an album in 2026. It also topped the Official Record Store Chart and the Official Vinyl Albums Chart.

pages.heading: Youth Night lights up clubs across the country
pages.body: On Friday 13 November, and the evenings either side, youth clubs and projects opened their doors for Oíche na hÓige. There were silent discos, drumming, art, coding, Lego robotics and virtual reality, plus podcasts and music made by young people. Minister Hildegarde Naughton visited Galway and said the atmosphere does not lie. In rugby, Ireland beat Argentina forty two to twelve.

pages.heading: December is already in the diary
pages.body: December has a few dates already confirmed. Dublin gets a week of film concerts at the RDS from 1 December. The Newgrange sun is due to be livestreamed on 21 December. Ireland's EU Presidency ends on 31 December, and Dublin sees in the new year with a three day festival. We will see you there.
